Simon set the recovered drive on the bedroom table and waited for Esther to ask why its seal was broken.

"But broken."

Simon retrieved the drive with two careful movements. One for the table, one for her view. "We had five hours to replace the data before the courier left."

"I could have done that in two." Esther traced his scar with her thumb, listening to his breathing change. "Or I could have explained why I never break my own seals."

Simon lowered his hand to where Esther touched him. "You were quiet this evening," he said. "Like someone still making decisions inside their head."

She waited another breath before answering. "Sometimes a conversation isn't a conversation. Sometimes it's the thing you can't change by talking about it."

Simon moved his hand up her arm. "I understood that," he said. "The service might have listened to us both. I decided that was more risk than we could afford."

Her finger remained against his chest as she spoke. "Counting aloud is an operational practice. This is a domestic one."

Esther drew the back of Simon's hand across her mouth. The movement traced scars. Her body relaxed when Simon followed the trail.

"Which decision are we making together now?" he asked.

"The house."

His thumb slid down Esther's cheek. "This morning?"

"Tonight."

She pressed his fingers against her scar.

Simon took a breath.

"We haven't spoken privately in six days," he said.

"Four." Her voice dropped below audible.

"I'm yours to question," he said.

She gave him a look that did not conceal pleasure.

He met her eyes before speaking. "I was counting the ways to tell you it wasn't safe here. I chose the one you wouldn't interrupt."

Esther let herself smile for two seconds.

"You're going to make me beg?" Simon said.

She took her finger from his chest and guided his hand beneath her skirt. The sound of her breathing changed.

He held his breath for three seconds, then spoke into her hair. "Tell me how."

"I told you the first time this house wasn't yours," she said.

"I remember that." He looked at her hand moving across him.

Esther brought Simon's index finger to her mouth and drew it in slowly. He released her wrist and put his hand beneath her neck when she bent her head toward his chest. His other hand rested on the bare skin of her hip, fingers spread wide.

Simon touched his forefinger with a warning look. "The drive."

She touched his cheek then covered the reminder. Her breath quickened.

"I never ask for that," he said.

Esther made a sound that wasn't agreement. She rested her forehead against his sternum while the rest of her body relaxed.

His breathing changed again.

She lifted her head and looked into his eyes. "You have to make this choice first."

Simon watched her fingers move. His hands remained steady on her waist as he reached for the drive beneath her hand. She let him take it and felt the tension in his shoulders shift as he set it aside.

Her eyes stayed on his as she rose onto her toes and kissed the junction between his jaw and neck. The sound he made was neither question nor answer.

Simon's hands closed more firmly on her waist when she opened his trousers and drew her finger across his cock. His breathing quickened. Esther watched him catch control of it.

His fingers tightened slightly. "How slow?" he asked.

Esther moved slowly, watching the pulse in Simon's throat. When her breath caught he leaned his head to kiss the top of her arm where the scar met skin again.

"There," she said.

He stopped.

Simon breathed against her back. His hand came to her breast where the scar ended. The other remained on her hip. She could feel the pulse in his wrist slow under her thumb.

"You're still watching," she said.

He looked directly into her eyes as he took a measured breath. "The drive."

"Still there," she said.

Another breath.

Simon waited until Esther made a sound of impatience and moved the finger at her hip to her clitoris. His hand tightened again as she drew in breath and closed her eyes.

The movement between them changed when her breathing deepened.

They were louder than before.

The house was still.

Afterward, Esther held the new drive close enough that Simon could have reached for it if he needed to. He watched her face as she breathed through the release of tension.

When she opened her eyes, he spoke softly. "Where did you find another?"

Esther touched his face with the back of her hand. "It wasn't from here." Her eyes remained on his as she continued. "The first drive had both our names attached to it. This one only has mine. My decision."
